Seconds since the server's bead cache last took in fresh data from its store: a full re-scan, or a write, event or row re-read it applied. It is the cache's age, not each row's, so it grows between re-scans and while the city is suspended. An endpoint reports it only when its body is read from the cache, and not every such endpoint does; 0 when this one does not, the store it read has no cache, or the cache has never been primed.

What bounds X-GC-Cache-Age-S. scheduled: the cache re-scans its store every X-GC-Cache-Refresh-Interval-S seconds. paused: the server has paused those re-scans while the city is suspended with no session running. failing: the cache's last re-scan of its store failed; it retries with backoff. rebuilding: the body is a response the server saved X-GC-Cache-Age-S seconds ago, served while it builds a fresh one. Omitted when the body was not read from a primed cache, except rebuilding: a saved /status response reports rebuilding whatever it was built from, and its X-GC-Cache-Refresh-Interval-S is then 0.
Seconds between the scheduled re-scans of its store by the bead cache X-GC-Cache-Age-S describes (its current adaptive cadence). 0 when the body was not read from a primed cache.

get.description: Ready work as `gc ready` answers it, read by the controller from the stores it already holds open, over the rigs of the config it has loaded. Every store is read live at request time (never from a read cache), so work that became ready before the request is in the answer. It reads the city store, the serving (non-suspended) rigs and any relocated class binding, merges them first-store-wins in that order, applies the filters, orders and cuts to the limit. Any store that cannot be read fails the whole request with 503 `store-unavailable`; there is no partial answer. A rig added, removed or rebound in the city's config takes effect in the answer at the controller's next config reload. While a config reload or API config write is in progress, or after a failed reload until one succeeds, the request is refused with 503 `service-unavailable`. Either 503 means the caller should read the stores in-process instead.
